name: Darkroom
description: A pro photo-grading darkroom: film looks, third-party .cube LUTs, design system colour treatments and finishing texture - then bake your look as a LUT any editor can use. Opens a Photoshop or GIMP file as layers too: position, blend and hide each one, grade the composite, and export flat images or a layered PSD.

featured.blurb: Grade photos with film looks, LUTs and your brand colours

inputs.label: Image
inputs.help: Pick a photo or SVG, or upload your own - vectors are rasterised on selection. Everything is processed on your device - the pixels never leave the browser. Leave empty to grade the lorikeet portrait that ships with the catalogue, or choose Use camera to grade a live feed.

inputs.label: Zoom & position
inputs.help: Drag the photo on the canvas to move it, scroll to zoom, and hold Alt while dragging to correct converging verticals. Or drag a label / type a value here.

inputs.label: Editing range
inputs.help: HDR keeps original precision and highlights while grading. The preview is tone mapped for SDR. Choose HDR separately when exporting. Up to 8 megapixels.

inputs.label: Layers
inputs.help: Bottom to top - later layers paint on top. Drop a PSD or XCF on the canvas (or use the gallery) to import a whole file; the composite feeds the grade below.

fields.label: X
fields.help: Left edge, in canvas pixels. Negative moves off-canvas.

fields.label: Group
fields.help: Folder path from the imported file (kept for PSD export).

inputs.label: Temperature
inputs.help: White balance: negative cools the image toward blue, positive warms it toward amber.

inputs.label: Tint
inputs.help: White balance: negative shifts toward green, positive toward magenta.

inputs.label: Exposure
inputs.help: Brightness in photographic stops (EV), applied in linear light like a camera.

inputs.label: Contrast
inputs.help: A smooth S-curve around mid-grey - push the tones apart or flatten them.

inputs.label: Highlights
inputs.help: Recover blown skies (negative) or push the bright end brighter (positive).

inputs.label: Shadows
inputs.help: Lift detail out of the darks (positive) or deepen them (negative).

inputs.label: Saturation
inputs.help: 0 = greyscale · 100 = original · 200 = vivid.

inputs.label: Vibrance
inputs.help: Smart saturation: boosts muted colours first and eases off where colour is already rich.

inputs.label: Dehaze
inputs.help: Cuts through haze: deeper blacks, more contrast and more colour. Negative values add a soft, hazy lift.

inputs.label: Levels channel
inputs.help: Which channel the five Levels sliders below adjust. Each colour channel is applied first, then RGB, as in Photoshop.

inputs.label: Input black
inputs.help: Every level at or below this becomes the output black.

inputs.label: Midtones
inputs.help: Gamma for the midtones. Above 1 brightens them, below 1 darkens them.

inputs.label: Input white
inputs.help: Every level at or above this becomes the output white.

inputs.label: Output black
inputs.help: The level the darkest tones map to. Raise it for a faded black.

inputs.label: Output white
inputs.help: The level the lightest tones map to. Lower it to soften the highlights.

inputs.label: Auto levels
inputs.help: Stretches each colour channel to this photo's own range, clipping its darkest and lightest 0.1%. The photo is measured again every time, so one look adapts to every photo in a batch. The Levels sliders adjust on top. Not used in HDR editing or with the live camera.

inputs.label: Curve channel
inputs.help: Which tone curve to edit. Each colour channel's curve is applied first, then the RGB curve.

inputs.label: RGB curve
inputs.help: Click the square to add a point, then drag points into place. Drag a point off the square, or press Delete, to remove that point. Each point is an input and an output level from 0 to 255, written as 0-0_64-48_255-255; empty is a straight line.

inputs.label: Colour mix
inputs.help: A Lightroom-style HSL mixer. Pick which property to adjust, then push each colour band. Hue rotates that band, Saturation makes it richer or greyer, Luminance brightens or darkens it. Only colours near each band move - greys stay put - and the whole mix bakes into the .cube LUT.

inputs.label: Convert to black & white
inputs.help: Converts to grey the way Photoshop's Black & White does: each family of colours has its own brightness, so reds and greens stay apart instead of flattening into one grey.

inputs.label: Reds
inputs.help: How bright reds become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Yellows
inputs.help: How bright yellows become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Greens
inputs.help: How bright greens become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Cyans
inputs.help: How bright cyans become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Blues
inputs.help: How bright blues become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Magentas
inputs.help: How bright magentas become in grey, as a percentage. The default is Photoshop's.

inputs.label: Tint
inputs.help: Colours the grey while keeping its tones, for a sepia or cyanotype print.

inputs.label: Tint hue
inputs.help: The tint's hue in degrees. 35 is a warm sepia; around 210 is a cyanotype blue.

inputs.label: Tint strength
inputs.help: How strongly the tint colours the grey.

inputs.label: Tones
inputs.help: Which tonal range the three sliders below shift. Each range fades into the next, so a shift never bands.

inputs.label: Cyan to red
inputs.help: Negative moves this range towards cyan, positive towards red.

inputs.label: Magenta to green
inputs.help: Negative moves this range towards magenta, positive towards green.

inputs.label: Yellow to blue
inputs.help: Negative moves this range towards yellow, positive towards blue.

inputs.label: Preserve luminosity
inputs.help: Keeps each pixel's brightness as it was, so only its colour moves.

inputs.label: Film look
inputs.help: Original film-inspired looks built from open, procedural curves - no sampled stock, so they're safe to ship anywhere.

inputs.label: Look strength
inputs.help: Blend between the untouched image (0) and the full look (100).

inputs.label: LUT source
inputs.help: Preset LUTs are open looks you can apply and also download (CC0, or CC BY where a creator is credited). Choose Upload for your own commercial or personal LUTs - those stay on your device and never travel in a share link, so a preset is what makes a look shareable in a URL.

inputs.label: Preset
inputs.help: Open, on-device LUTs. The film-emulation looks are CC0 (no attribution needed); SUSE7 S-Log3 (Heavy) is a cinema grade for Sony S-Log3 footage, © SUSE by Peter Chamalian, under CC BY 4.0 (credit SUSE · Peter Chamalian). Applied with tetrahedral interpolation, and downloadable below for any editor.

inputs.label: LUT file (.cube / .3dl)
inputs.help: Load your own colour LUT - Adobe/IRIDAS .cube (1D or 3D) or Autodesk .3dl. Applied on your device with tetrahedral interpolation, after Develop and the film look. Your file never leaves the browser, and an uploaded LUT is not part of a share link.

inputs.label: LUT intensity
inputs.help: Blend between the un-LUTted image (0) and the full LUT (100).

inputs.label: Download this LUT (.cube)
inputs.help: Save the selected open preset as a .cube for DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut or Photoshop. These LUTs are public domain (CC0) - see the tool's NOTICE. The switch flips itself back off.

inputs.label: Baked LUT size
inputs.help: Grid size of the .cube this tool bakes. 33 is the industry default and loads everywhere.

inputs.label: Download look as .cube
inputs.help: Bakes the whole colour pipeline - Develop, film look, the preset or uploaded LUT and colour treatment - into one .cube LUT for DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut or Photoshop, and downloads it. The switch flips itself back off. Texture effects (grain, vignette…) are spatial and can't live in a LUT.

inputs.label: Treatment
inputs.help: Colour treatments seeded from the design system palette. Leave the colours below empty to auto-pick from its tokens; set them to override.

inputs.label: Treatment amount
inputs.help: Blend between the untreated image (0) and the full treatment (100).

inputs.label: Shadow colour
inputs.help: Empty = auto: the darkest colour in the design system palette.

inputs.label: Midtone colour
inputs.help: Empty = auto: the most colourful swatch in the design system palette.

inputs.label: Highlight colour
inputs.help: Empty = auto: the lightest colour in the design system palette.

inputs.label: Film grain
inputs.help: Seeded, luminance-weighted monochrome grain - strongest in the midtones, like real stock.

inputs.label: Grain size
inputs.help: Clump size of the grain in pixels.

inputs.label: Vignette
inputs.help: Gently darken the corners to pull the eye inward.

inputs.label: Bloom
inputs.help: Soft glow spilling from the brightest areas.

inputs.label: Halation
inputs.help: The warm red-orange halo film prints around hot highlights.

inputs.label: Colour fringing
inputs.help: Lens-style colour fringing that grows toward the corners.

inputs.label: Sharpen
inputs.help: Unsharp-mask crispness. A little goes a long way.

inputs.label: Dust & scratches
inputs.help: Seeded specks, fibres and hairline scratches - the imperfections of a well-loved print.

inputs.label: Seed
inputs.help: Re-rolls the grain and dust patterns. The same seed always gives the same result.

inputs.label: Before / after split
inputs.help: Lay the untouched image over the graded result behind a divider you can drag and rotate. A raster export bakes the divider exactly as placed - handy for approval decks.

inputs.label: Histogram
inputs.help: Live RGB + luminance histogram over the canvas. Screen only - never part of the export.
